title: Classify four physical plant responses before modelling
equipment: Modular skid with heated vessel, buffer tank, conveyor oven, and flexible drive
physicalPurpose: Distinguish self-regulating, integrating, delayed, and oscillatory dynamics from bounded open-loop evidence before choosing a model or controller.
objective: Apply one normalized bounded experiment to four physical modules and classify each response from measured signatures without fitting a model.

simplifications: Each module isolates one dominant signature; real equipment can combine regulation, integration, delay, and oscillation.
The common normalized experiment command is mapped to different physical actuator units and is not plotted as a substitute for those commands.
No controller, model fit, or configured model label is used to produce the learner's classification.

baseline.limitation: A short view makes slow, delayed, and integrating traces appear compatible with the same low-gain stable process assumption.

change.decision: Observe long enough to measure equilibrium tendency, continuing slope, response delay, overshoot, and crossings before fitting or tuning.

abortPredicates: Any command or PV is nonfinite or outside its hard limit
Physical command mapping differs between compared runs
A feedback controller is active during the open-loop experiment
safety.restorationMode: Return normalized experiment command to zero and restore all four initial operating points
safety.physicalApprovalRole: authorised process and machinery controls engineer
simulationOnlyRestrictions: The combined open-loop run is simulation-only. A physical test requires a separately reviewed safe step, duration, abort boundary, and authority for each plant.

video.viewerOutcome: Classify four physical plant responses from open-loop signatures before selecting a model or controller.

learning.context: A modular training skid contains a heated vessel, buffer tank, conveyor oven, and flexible drive whose early trends can look deceptively similar.
learning.reason: Lesson 31 assumed known plant classes. An unfamiliar loop must be classified from sufficient evidence before model or controller selection.
theory: Self-regulating output approaches a finite equilibrium; integrating output retains slope; delayed output initially remains unchanged; oscillatory output crosses its eventual value as stored energy exchanges.
Operating point, physical scaling, control direction, observation duration, sensor resolution, and excitation are part of the classification evidence.
Late slope, first response time, overshoot, and crossing count distinguish classes more reliably than one final sample.
Real plants may combine signatures, so an isolated teaching classification is a starting hypothesis rather than universal truth.
learning.workedPrediction: The vessel predicts 54 degC equilibrium and 53.93 degC at 12 s; the tank predicts 62 cm with 1 cm/s slope; the oven predicts 4 s delay and 84.91 degC at 12 s; the drive predicts 52.7 percent overshoot around 1 rad.
practicalPreparation: Verify open-loop Manual authority, initial operating points, normalized-to-physical scaling, units, limits, quality, 100 ms sampling, 12 s duration, aborts, and simulation label.
Sketch four physical responses and state observable classification criteria before applying the step; hide configured model labels.
learning.baseline: Inspect only the first second and record which traces remain ambiguous.
learning.change: Run the full 12-second bounded step once, retain exact commands and PVs, classify each trace, and reveal labels only after committing the decision.
learning.comparison: Compare response delay, late slope, steady-value eligibility, overshoot, and crossing count in real units. Do not compare unlike PV amplitudes as if normalization removed their physics.
learning.validation: Require a finite vessel equilibrium tendency, tank slope near 1 cm/s, oven delay at least 3.9 s, drive peak at least 1.4 rad, and at least two drive crossings.
learning.explanation: The four signatures arise from loss-balanced energy, accumulated mass, transport delay, and exchanged mechanical energy respectively.
learning.transfer: Lesson 33 derives heater and tank behavior from conservation laws so their observed signatures become explainable predictions.
